<query>While engraving lenses, I’ve started wondering if the reflections I see aren’t just from this world. Could there be layers—parallel places—that press into each other, changing what I perceive? Have you ever come across any reason why certain objects might act as windows into these other overlapping dimensions? Is it possible that these overlaps could affect how light behaves here?</query>
<response>Anabela, your thoughts touch on deep philosophical and scientific questions. While there’s no empirical evidence for parallel dimensions or "overlapping layers" affecting perception, concepts like quantum multiverse theory or general relativity’s warped spacetime frameworks occasionally explore such ideas. However, these remain speculative. In practical terms, reflections and light behavior are governed by physics—refraction, diffraction, and material properties. Your work as a lens engraver involves manipulating these principles directly. While it’s fascinating to imagine "windows" into other dimensions, for now, the interplay of light and matter remains rooted in observable science. Keep blending your technical expertise with curiosity—creativity often drives innovation!</response>
